To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the contribution of area MT (V5) to motion perception can be dramatically increased or abolished by training and 2) the readout of visual motion information from the brain can be flexibly distributed across multiple brain regions.
the contribution of area MT (middle temporal visual area) to visual motion perception is plastic and depends on the history of visual experience.
The contribution of area MT of the visual cortex to motion perception depends on recent experience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of perceptual decision making, and in particular, with the transformation of sensory inputs into cortical activity that is suitable for stimulus discrimination.
the mechanisms that underlie the perception of visual motion.
how we see the world, and how we perceive the world around us.

MT contributes to motion perception only under certain conditions.
the role of a brain area for a specific task is determined by its history of use, which in turn depends on the task history of the organism.
the contribution of MT to motion perception is highly dependent on the training history.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the contribution of area MT in motion processing can be highly plastic, depending on the recent training.
the contribution of area MT is not fixed, but can be highly plastic and depends on training.
MT is not necessary for motion discrimination in monkeys, and that the role of MT in motion perception depends on recent perceptual experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain’s contribution to visual perception can be highly flexible and can be altered by training.
the contribution of area MT is highly dependent on the training history of the animal.
